params.script_inline:
import sys, json, re, hashlib, datetime

# The front door of a colony that talks to many channels. One question per
# turn: has this channel been here before? A channel with a ledger row is
# handed through on the lane its own talky answers to; a channel without one
# gets a talky of its own -- instantiated by ONE mutation that carries the node
# AND every crossing port edge, because an island without a crossing edge
# derives inactive and never wakes.
#
# The cell is SELF-LOCATING: `target` is its own path, so the scope of the
# mutation is the hive's parent and nothing has to be configured twice.

doc = json.load(sys.stdin)
d = doc["body"]
envelope = doc["envelope"]
h = envelope.get("header", {})
ctx = h.get("context", {})
hop = h.get("hop", {})
lane = str(hop.get("route", ""))
phase = str(ctx.get("rec_phase", ""))
op = hop.get("operation")
# `operation` says WHICH op answered, `error_code` says WHETHER it worked, and
# both have to be read (GH #343).
err = str(hop.get("error_code", "") or "")

SELF = str(envelope.get("target", "") or "")
# The provider lane, and the only environment token left in this cell: a
# model id belongs to the deployment, not to the instance (convention
# K-H2, lane B -- the RESOLVED literal goes in `.env`, never a nested
# token).
MODEL = "${RECEPTIONIST_MODEL:-openai/gpt-4o-mini}"

# Everything else is this cell's OWN configuration, and it arrives on the
# same stdin document: `params` is one of its three top-level objects,
# beside `envelope` and `body`, and the substrate always sets it ({} when
# there is nothing to hand over). So each knob below is per-INSTANCE
# configuration -- two receptions of one colony build different composites
# and answer onto different lanes, and a mutation retunes one of them
# without touching a colony-wide environment (GH #138). The literal beside
# each name is the shipped default; it is the same value the template
# config and `contract.settings` carry, and a test pins the three against
# each other.
P = doc.get("params") or {}


def _knob(key, default):
    # A knob explicitly set to null is "not configured", not a crash: an
    # operator who blanks a line in a config means the default.
    v = P.get(key, default)
    return default if v is None else v


def _str(key, default):
    # No blank-string fallback here, deliberately: for an ADDRESS knob the empty
    # string is a VALUE. Six of the seven below ship EMPTY and mean something
    # by it -- an empty ingress or reply_from is the instance path itself, an
    # empty target leaves that edge out of the mutation -- so a "helpful"
    # fallback would make the shipped default unsayable. Only null is "not
    # configured".
    return str(_knob(key, default))


TEMPLATE = _str("template", "talky")
INGRESS = _str("ingress", "")
REPLY_FROM = _str("reply_from", "")
ERROR_FROM = _str("error_from", "")
REPLY_TO = _str("reply_to", "")
WRITE_TO = _str("write_to", "")
ERROR_TO = _str("error_to", "")

now = datetime.datetime.now(datetime.timezone.utc).strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S.%fZ")
COLUMNS = ["channel", "talky_path", "created_at"]

# The round the conversation is spoken in. It is DECLARED by the caller's
# ingress edge and it is a constant of the generation this turn opens (ADR-0002
# E8), so the door is the only place it can come from -- and this cell HAS no
# other place: a channel identity is a room, not a participant, and turning one
# into the other would invent a member nobody named. A door that declares
# nothing leaves it EMPTY: never derived from the channel, never ["*"], and the
# write path refuses the untagged day rather than storing it as everyone's.
audience = ""


def round_of(value):
    """A set travels as a JSON string; a native list in the context is taken
    too, and re-serialised rather than stringified."""
    if isinstance(value, (list, dict)):
        return json.dumps(value)
    return str(value or "")


def park():
    """Terminal by design. The greet sits in the ingress path of a loop and in
    front of a mutation lane: anything it cannot name is parked, never echoed."""
    sys.stdout.write(json.dumps([]))
    sys.exit(0)


def emit(msgs):
    sys.stdout.write(json.dumps(msgs))
    sys.exit(0)


def rows_of(doc):
    msgs = doc.get("messages", [])
    if not msgs:
        return []
    try:
        rows = json.loads(msgs[0].get("text", "[]"))
    except Exception:
        return []
    return rows if isinstance(rows, list) else []


def key_of(channel):
    """A channel identity is free text; a node name and a CEL string literal
    are not. The key is the sanitised form -- and a channel that HAD to be
    sanitised keeps a digest of the original, so `tg:42` and `tg/42` can never
    collapse onto one talky."""
    safe = re.sub(r"[^A-Za-z0-9_-]", "_", channel)
    if safe == channel and safe != "":
        return safe
    digest = hashlib.sha1(channel.encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()[:8]
    return (safe or "ch") + "-" + digest


def places():
    """scope, hive. The hive is the cell's parent, the scope is the hive's
    parent: a receptionist at /main/front/greet mutates /main and addresses
    itself as ./front.

    The HIVE, never this cell (GH #228): the reception is sealed, so an edge out
    of `./front/greet` is a breach the mutation validation refuses, and the turn
    leaves on the `turn` lane at the hive path anyway. Which cell produced it is
    not something the edge it draws is allowed to know -- including when the
    cell drawing it is that cell."""
    segs = [s for s in SELF.split("/") if s]
    if len(segs) < 2:
        return "/", "./" + (segs[-1] if segs else "greet")
    return "/" + "/".join(segs[:-2]), "./" + segs[-2]


def store_op(args, ph, channel, keep=""):
    """Every emission carries the full key set the hive edges read. A missing
    hop key makes a CEL modifier fail, and a failed modifier SKIPS the edge --
    so keys are always present and empty rather than absent."""
    return {"header": {"route": "rstore", "phase": ph, "channel": channel,
                       "chan": "", "chan_raw": "", "aud": audience,
                       "rec_body": keep},
            "messages": [{"origin": "assistant", "type": "tool_call",
                          "id": "r-" + ph, "text": json.dumps(args)}]}


def turn_msg(channel, keep):
    """The turn on its channel lane. `chan` is the safe key the edge condition
    compares, `chan_raw` the identity the keeper downstream should mint ids
    from -- carrying both is what keeps the condition free of escaping."""
    m = {"header": {"route": "turn", "phase": "", "channel": channel,
                    "chan": key_of(channel), "chan_raw": channel,
                    "aud": audience, "rec_body": ""}}
    m.update(keep)
    return m


def node_of(channel):
    scope, _ = places()
    node = TEMPLATE + "-" + key_of(channel)
    return node, (("" if scope == "/" else scope) + "/" + node)


def mutation_for(channel):
    """ONE mutation: the talky AND all four crossing port edges. Order inside
    the diff is irrelevant (the colony validates the post-state), but the
    edges MUST travel with the node -- a subtree without a crossing edge
    derives inactive and its timer never spawns."""
    scope, self_rel = places()
    key = key_of(channel)
    node, _ = node_of(channel)
    base = "./" + node

    def at(seg):
        """The composite's own path, or a sub-path under it.

        Since GH #228 every shipped composite is sealed (`params.ports: []`),
        so the entry, the reply and the error drain are LANES at the instance
        path and the three settings default to empty. A non-empty setting still
        names a sub-path, for a composite that has not been sealed -- an address
        the boundary refuses is the caller's to fix, not this cell's to guess.
        """
        return base + "/" + seg if seg else base

    edges = [{
        "from": self_rel,
        "to": at(INGRESS),
        "condition": ("has(hop.route) && hop.route == 'turn' && "
                      "has(hop.chan) && hop.chan == '" + key + "'"),
        "modifier": {"set_hop": {"route": "'in_turn'"},
                     "set_context": {"channel": "hop.chan_raw",
                                     "audience_set": "hop.aud"}},
    }]
    if REPLY_TO:
        # Three sorts travel talky's answer lane and only ONE of them is an
        # answer: a real one, a round that hit max_iter (hop.round_capped) and
        # -- since collector@2.1.1 -- a turn the store would not let be
        # assembled (hop.degraded, GH #343). The second and third carry no
        # answer to say, so neither reaches the reply sink; guarding on
        # round_capped ALONE let the third through, and a store refusal read to
        # a person reads as a real reply. Both dead-letter loudly instead,
        # which is where this template already leaves the capped sort.
        edges.append({"from": at(REPLY_FROM), "to": REPLY_TO,
                      "condition": ("has(hop.route) && hop.route == 'answer' && "
                                    "!has(hop.round_capped) && "
                                    "!has(hop.degraded)")})
    if WRITE_TO:
        edges.append({"from": at(REPLY_FROM), "to": WRITE_TO,
                      "condition": "has(hop.route) && hop.route == 'write'",
                      "modifier": {"set_hop": {"route": "'in_batch'"}}})
    if ERROR_TO:
        edges.append({"from": at(ERROR_FROM), "to": ERROR_TO,
                      "condition": "has(hop.route) && hop.route == 'error'"})
    return {"header": {"msg_type": "mutation", "route": "mutate", "phase": "",
                       "channel": channel, "chan": key, "chan_raw": channel,
                       "aud": audience, "rec_body": ""},
            "messages": [],
            "scope": scope,
            "diff": {"add_nodes": [{"name": node, "template": TEMPLATE}],
                     "add_edges": edges},
            "ctx": {"model": MODEL}}


# ==================================================================== VERDICT
# A colony reply is not a UBF body and carries neither context nor correlation.
# It is TERMINAL here: reading "anything that is not a request" as a request is
# the reply-fallback loop that spins until the TTL kills it. A rejected
# mutation needs no repair either -- the only reject this lane produces is a
# name collision, which means the channel got its talky from the turn that
# raced this one, and that talky answers the same key.
if "mutation" in d:
    park()

# ================================================================== REFUSED
# A store refusal is not a result. It sits after the mutation guard -- a colony
# reply carries an error_code but never an `operation`, so the two cannot be
# confused -- and ahead of the lanes and the phases.
#
# Measured before the guard existed: a refused `look` came back as an empty row
# list, the branch below read that as "a channel nobody has met", and the
# reception emitted a MUTATION that grows a SECOND agent for a channel that
# already has one, plus a duplicate ledger row. "The ledger did not answer" and
# "this channel is new" are the same shape and opposite facts, and only one of
# them may build a tree.
#
# The two steps do not leave the same thing standing, and the text says which
# one this was. The `open` insert is fire-and-forget -- it rides in the SAME
# emission as the mutation and the turn -- so by the time its refusal arrives
# the agent exists and the turn is already on its lane.
if err and op:
    if str(ctx.get("rec_phase", "")) == "open":
        state = ("the agent WAS built and the turn already left on its own "
                 "lane; only the ledger row is missing. Every later turn on "
                 "this channel therefore repeats the instantiation, and the "
                 "colony refuses each repeat as a name collision -- the "
                 "conversation works, the reception is noisy forever")
    else:
        state = ("no agent was built and no row was written -- an unanswered "
                 "lookup is not a channel nobody has met")
    emit([{"header": {"route": "reject", "reject_reason": "store_refused",
                      "store_error": err, "store_operation": str(op),
                      "phase": "",
                      "channel": str(ctx.get("rec_channel", "")
                                     or ctx.get("channel", "") or ""),
                      "chan": "", "chan_raw": "", "aud": "", "rec_body": ""},
           "messages": [{"origin": "tool", "type": "tool_result", "id": "r-reject",
                         "text": "the channel ledger refused the " + str(op)
                                 + " of step '" + str(ctx.get("rec_phase", ""))
                                 + "': " + err + ". " + state}]}])

# ==================================================================== LANES
if lane == "in_turn":
    if op is not None:
        park()
    channel = str(ctx.get("channel", "") or hop.get("channel", "") or "default")
    audience = round_of(ctx.get("audience_set", ""))
    # The turn rides through the lookup on the hop: a store reply carries the
    # row, not the conversation that asked for it.
    emit([store_op({"operation": "select", "table": "channels",
                    "columns": COLUMNS, "where": {"channel": channel},
                    "limit": 1}, "look", channel, json.dumps(d))])

if lane:
    park()

# =================================================================== PHASES
if phase == "look" and op == "select" and not err:
    channel = str(ctx.get("rec_channel", "") or "default")
    audience = round_of(ctx.get("rec_aud", ""))
    rows = rows_of(d)
    try:
        keep = json.loads(str(ctx.get("rec_body", "") or "{}"))
    except Exception:
        keep = {}
    if not isinstance(keep, dict):
        keep = {}
    keep.setdefault("messages", [])
    if rows:
        # Known channel: straight through on its own lane, no mutation.
        emit([turn_msg(channel, keep)])
    # New channel. Three emissions, and the ORDER is the whole trick: the
    # mutation is dispatched inline by the colony's outputs arm before the next
    # emission is taken from the mailbox, so the ingress edge it draws is
    # already in the edge table when the turn behind it is routed. The turn
    # that triggered the instantiation is therefore never lost.
    _, talky_path = node_of(channel)
    emit([mutation_for(channel),
          store_op({"operation": "insert", "table": "channels",
                    "row": {"channel": channel, "talky_path": talky_path,
                            "created_at": now}}, "open", channel),
          turn_msg(channel, keep)])

park()

model.description: RECEPTIONIST_MODEL -- the provider model id handed to every talky this cell instantiates, as ctx.model. The one knob of this cell that stays in the environment: a model id belongs to the deployment (ruling R-0904-6). Convention K-H2 (Lane B): put the RESOLVED literal in .env, not a nested token.

template.description: The composite instantiated per channel. It also names the instances: <template>-<channel key>.

ingress.description: Where the turn enters the composite, relative to the instance root. EMPTY (the default) is the instance path itself, which is what a sealed composite wants: since GH #228 talky declares `params.ports: []`, so the address is the hive and the lane the edge sets (`in_turn`) is what selects the cell behind the door. Set it only for a composite that is not sealed. Blanking it is a VALUE, not an omission -- only null means 'not configured'.

reply_from.description: Where answers and write batches leave the composite, relative to the instance root. EMPTY (the default) is the instance path itself; the lanes are `answer`, `write` and `error` on `hop.route`.

error_from.description: Where the composite's error lane leaves, relative to the instance root. EMPTY (the default) is the instance path itself.

reply_to.description: Scope-relative target of the answer lane. Empty means the edge is left out and the answers dead-letter.

write_to.description: Scope-relative target of the closed-session batch. Empty means the edge is left out.

error_to.description: Scope-relative target of the error drain. Empty means the edge is left out.

description.purpose: The front door: it asks the ledger which channel a turn belongs to, hands a known channel through to the talky that already answers it, and gives an unknown channel a talky of its own -- one mutation, node plus all crossing port edges, and the triggering turn right behind it.
description.use_when: In front of a fleet of per-channel agents, between the surface and the talkys. One per colony. The parent writes TWO edges: the ingress into ./greet, and the PRIVILEGED lane ./greet -> /colony/mutations, which only a bootstrap config.json can grant.
description.not_in_scope: No conversation, no persona, no tools: what the agent is belongs to the composite. It never removes an instance (No-Delete), never routes an answer itself, and never decides what a channel IS or who is in the room -- the ingress edge promotes both, and a channel identity is never turned into a participant identity.
description.emits_meaning: route rstore: the ledger ops of the current step (hop.phase carries the step, hop.channel the identity, hop.aud the round, hop.rec_body the turn in transit -- all promoted to context by the hive edge, the round as context.rec_aud). route mutate (hop.msg_type mutation): the instantiation, for the privileged lane only. route turn: the inbound turn, unchanged, on the channel lane -- hop.chan is the safe key the edge compares, hop.chan_raw the identity the composite should mint session ids from, and hop.aud the round the door declared, which the drawn ingress edge promotes to context.audience_set. All three are always present and empty when unknown. route reject: the channel ledger refused an op of this chain (hop.reject_reason 'store_refused', hop.store_error the ledger's own error_code -- a free string, because the store's code list is open -- and hop.store_operation the refused op). The body names the STEP: at 'look' NOTHING is built and nothing is written (an unanswered lookup is not a channel nobody has met, and before this guard existed it grew a second agent for one that was already here); at 'open' the agent was already built and the turn already left in the same emission, so only the ledger row is missing -- and every later turn on that channel then repeats the instantiation, which the colony refuses as a name collision (GH #343).
description.consumes_meaning: One entry lane, named by hop.route on the port edge: in_turn, with context.channel naming the room and context.audience_set naming the round it is spoken in (a JSON list in affinity vocabulary; a native list is taken too). Neither is derived from the other, and neither is defaulted -- an undeclared round stays empty all the way to the generation row. The ledger reply is dispatched by context.rec_phase together with hop.operation. A body carrying `mutation` is the colony's verdict and is terminal -- which is why consumes.body is EMPTY: a colony reply is not a UBF body and would bounce against any declared key.
examples: in_turn on an unknown channel tg:42 -> one mutation (add_nodes talky-tg_42-<digest> + 4 port edges, the ingress one promoting channel AND audience_set), one ledger insert, and the turn on lane 'turn'
in_turn on a known channel -> exactly the turn; the edge the earlier mutation drew takes it to that channel's talky
